charter.title: What lyrid keeps
charter.lede: The sky is public and works without an account. An account remembers what is listed below across your machines, and this page is the whole list — not a summary of one.

noAccount.heading: If you have no account
noAccount.body: Nothing about you is stored on the server. Your marker's shape and colour live in your own browser, and the view you are looking at lives in the address bar. Neither reaches us.

withAccount.heading: If you do
withAccount.addressBody: To sign you in, and to send you a way back if you lose your password. The only other mail is the weekly letter, and only if you ask for it. No announcements.
withAccount.place: Where you left the sky, and how you like your marked star drawn.
withAccount.placeBody: The reason an account is worth having.
withAccount.sessionsBody: A random token per browser, so signing out actually ends the session rather than waiting for it to expire.
withAccount.listening: If you link ListenBrainz: its account name, and every listen it holds.
withAccount.listeningBody: For each listen, when it was, which artists it was by (their MusicBrainz ids), how long it ran and the light it gathered — none for listens from before the link — and no track or album names. Your listens are already public on ListenBrainz; this copy exists only so your own sky can show what you have heard. The token you paste to link is checked once and never kept. Unlinking stops the reading; what was gathered stays until you delete the account.
withAccount.lastfm: If you bring a Last.fm file: the listens it names.
withAccount.lastfmBody: When each was, and the artist if lyrid can place them; the track's name only to tell one scrobble from another, folded into an id and not kept. The file itself is read and dropped. You can forget everything a file brought at any time.
withAccount.born: If you give it: the year you were born.
withAccount.bornBody: Only the year. It becomes the six years you were fifteen to twenty, and the sky is asked about those years, not about you.
withAccount.letter: If you ask for the weekly letter: that you asked, and in which language.
withAccount.letterBody: And a random key in the link that stops it without signing in. Stopping it removes all of this.

counted.heading: What is counted, and what is not
counted.body: How often each part of lyrid gets used is counted — how many times the radio was opened on a given day, not who opened it. The counters are numbers that go up. There is no row per event, so there is nothing to join back to a person, and no clever query later can turn these into a history of what you looked at.
counted.never: What lyrid does not do: use your listening for anything but your own sky, sell or share anything with anyone, run third-party analytics or advertising, or track you across other sites.

whose.heading: Whose sky is it
whose.body: The map itself is built from open data — MusicBrainz, ListenBrainz, Discogs, Wikidata and Wikipedia — and belongs to nobody. Your account holds no part of it. What rises in it each week is counted from everyone’s listening on ListenBrainz, from the dump ListenBrainz publishes every day — not from the listening lyrid keeps for your own sky, which serves nothing else.

listening.heading: Listening
listening.pitch: What you listen to anywhere opens its stars here and gathers light.
listening.linkBody: Whatever you play that scrobbles to ListenBrainz opens its stars here and gathers light — new music far more than old favourites. Your whole history is read first, so the sky lights up with everything you have heard; light is gathered from the moment you link.
